arxiv-2007-03152.description: Abstract . The open-source and community-supported gem5 simulator is one of the most popular tools for computer architecture research. This simulation infrastructure allows researchers to model modern computer hardware at the cycle level, and it has enough fidelity to boot unmodified Linux-based operating systems and run full applications for multiple architectures including x86, Arm®, and RISC-V.

arxiv-2106-08588.title: Anomalous transport in Kane fermions
arxiv-2106-08588.creator: Karun Gadge, Sumanta Tewari, Girish Sharma
arxiv-2106-08588.description: Abstract Kane fermions are characterized by a linear Dirac cone intersecting with a flat band, resembling a pseudo-spin-1 Dirac semimetal. Similar to relativistic Dirac fermions, Kane fermions satisfy a linear energy-momentum relation and can be classified as being pseudo-relativistic. Though not protected by symmetry or by topology, Kane fermions can emerge by suitable band engineering, for example, in mercury-telluride compounds.

arxiv-2106-11696.title: Diversity-aware k k -median: Clustering with fair center representation Thanks: This research is supported by the Academy of Finland projects AIDA (317085) and MLDB (325117), the ERC Advanced Grant REBOUND (834862), the EC H2020 RIA project SoBigData (871042), and the Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Syste
arxiv-2106-11696.creator: Suhas Thejaswi, Bruno Ordozgoiti, Aristides Gionis
arxiv-2106-11696.description: Abstract We introduce a novel problem for diversity-aware clustering. We assume that the potential cluster centers belong to a set of groups defined by protected attributes, such as ethnicity, gender, etc. We then ask to find a minimum-cost clustering of the data into k k clusters so that a specified minimum number of cluster centers are chosen from each group.

arxiv-2201-01789.title: Tensor renormalization of three-dimensional Potts model
arxiv-2201-01789.creator: Raghav G. Jha
arxiv-2201-01789.description: Abstract Abstract: We study the q q -state Potts models on a cubic lattice in the thermodynamic limit using tensor renormalization group transformations with the triad approximation. By computing the thermodynamic potentials, we locate the first-order phase transitions for 10 < q ≤ 20 10<q\leq 20 which has not been explored using any method.

arxiv-2202-00990.title: Dictionary Learning for Clustering on Hyperspectral Images
arxiv-2202-00990.creator: Joshua Bruton, Hairong Wang
arxiv-2202-00990.description: Abstract Dictionary learning and sparse coding have been widely studied as mechanisms for unsupervised feature learning. Unsupervised learning could bring enormous benefit to the processing of hyperspectral images and to other remote sensing data analysis because labelled data is often scarce in this field.

arxiv-2209-15339.title: A Lagrangian model for drifting ecosystems reveals heterogeneity-driven enhancement of marine plankton blooms
arxiv-2209-15339.creator: Enrico Ser-Giacomi, Ricardo Martinez-Garcia, Stephanie Dutkiewicz, Michael J. Follows
arxiv-2209-15339.description: Abstract Marine plankton play a crucial role in carbon storage, oxygen production, global climate, and ecosystem function. Planktonic ecosystems are embedded in a Lagrangian patches of water that are continuously moving, stretching, and diluting. These processes drive inhomegeneities on a range of scales, with implications for the integrated ecosystem properties, but are hard to characterize.

arxiv-2310-10375.title: GTA: A Geometry-Aware Attention Mechanism for Multi-View Transformers
arxiv-2310-10375.creator: Takeru Miyato, Bernhard Jaeger, Max Welling, Andreas Geiger
arxiv-2310-10375.description: Abstract As transformers are equivariant to the permutation of input tokens, encoding the positional information of tokens is necessary for many tasks. However, since existing positional encoding schemes have been initially designed for NLP tasks, their suitability for vision tasks, which typically exhibit different structural properties in their data, is questionable.

arxiv-2310-18050.title: Non-existence of radial eigenfunctions for the perturbed Heisenberg sublaplacian
arxiv-2310-18050.creator: Luca Fanelli, Haruya Mizutani, Luz Roncal, Nico Michele Schiavone
arxiv-2310-18050.description: Abstract . We prove uniform resolvent estimates in weighted L 2 L^{2} -spaces for radial solutions of the sublaplacian ℒ \mathcal{L} on the Heisenberg group H d \mathbb{H}^{d} . The proofs are based on the multipliers methods, and strongly rely on the use of suitable multipliers and of the associated Hardy inequalities.

arxiv-2405-14514.title: Quantum Mpemba Effect in Random Circuits
arxiv-2405-14514.creator: Xhek Turkeshi, Pasquale Calabrese, Andrea De Luca
arxiv-2405-14514.description: Abstract The essence of the Mpemba effect is that non-equilibrium systems may relax faster the further they are from their equilibrium configuration. In the quantum realm, this phenomenon arises in the dynamics of closed systems, where it is witnessed by fundamental features such as symmetry and entanglement.

arxiv-2506-05020.creator: Haokun Liu, Zhaoqi Ma, Yunong Li, Junichiro Sugihara, Yicheng Chen, Jinjie Li, Moju Zhao
arxiv-2506-05020.description: Abstract Heterogeneous multi-robot systems show great potential in complex tasks requiring coordinated hybrid cooperation. However, traditional approaches relying on static models often struggle with task diversity and dynamic environments. This highlights the need for generalizable intelligence that can bridge high-level reasoning with low-level execution across heterogeneous agents.

arxiv-2507-05120.title: Experimental data re-uploading with provable enhanced learning capabilities
arxiv-2507-05120.creator: Martin F. X. Mauser, Solène Four, Lena Marie Predl, Riccardo Albiero, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Philipp Petersen, Borivoje Dakić, Iris Agresti, Philip Walther
arxiv-2507-05120.description: Abstract The last decades have seen the development of quantum machine learning, stemming from the intersection of quantum computing and machine learning. This field is particularly promising for the design of alternative quantum (or quantum inspired) computation paradigms that could require fewer resources with respect to standard ones, e.g. in terms of energy consumption.

pmc-11340961.title: Stroke rehabilitation in urban and rural settings in the Philippines: Protocol for an interview and visual elicitation study
pmc-11340961.creator: Sarah Ann Buckingham, Alyssa Marie Dar Juan, Sara Demain, June Ann De Vera, Myrna Estrada, Lorraine Hermosura-Faeldon, Bridie Kent, Maria Teresa Sharon Linog, Roy Francis Navea, Fiona Jones, on behalf of the TULAY project team, Johanna Pruller, Johanna Pruller
pmc-11340961.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionThere is a lack of community-based rehabilitation for stroke in the Philippines, and research on this topic is limited. Different challenges may be encountered in urban and rural settings. The aim of the Tulong, Ugnayan ng Lingap At gabaY (TULAY) project is to develop a context-appropriate, community-based stroke support programme, consisting of self-management and training resources to augment the rehabilitation and recovery process.

pmc-11448238.title: Resolved genomes of wastewater ESBL-producing Escherichia coli and metagenomic analysis of source wastewater samples
pmc-11448238.creator: Clinton Cheney, Jared D. Johnson, John P. Ste. Marie, Kayla Y. M. Gacosta, Natalie B. Denlinger Drumm, Gerrad D. Jones, Joy Waite-Cusic, Tala Navab-Daneshmand
pmc-11448238.description: Extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli pose a serious threat to human health because of their resistance to the most commonly prescribed antibiotics: penicillins and cephalosporins. In this study, we provide a genomic and metagenomic context for the determinant beta-lactam resistance genes of ESBL-positive E. coli isolated from various wastewater treatment utilities in Oregon, USA.

pmc-11580145.title: Methodologies and challenges in Arctic human health risk assessment: case studies and evaluation of current practices
pmc-11580145.creator: Khaled Abass, Alexey A Dudarev, Bryan Adlard, Zoe Gillespie, Arja Rautio, Luke Nych, Cheryl Khoury
pmc-11580145.description: In Arctic populations, a primary route of exposure to contaminants is through the diet. The health risks associated with these exposures can be characterised by conducting human health risk assessments. However, while there is guidance from many international and national organisations, there are limited examples of human health risk assessment in the Arctic.

pmc-12525859.title: Efficient Tissue Culture Method Based on Clustered Bud Proliferation for Producing High-Quality Arundo donax Seedlings

pmc-12525859.description: For its rapid growth, high yield, and broad adaptability, Arundo donax is widely used in various applications, yielding considerable economic and ecological benefits. However, widespread cultivation is challenging because A. donax can only be propagated asexually. In this study, a tissue culture method was developed using the clustered bud proliferation pathway.

pmc-12688002.title: Dexmedetomidine as an adjunct to local anesthetics for impacted third molar surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12688002.creator: Malik Alkabazi, Ebtesam Aldieb, Heba Hussein, Selvakumar Haridoss, Melek Tassoker, Gustavo Vicentis Oliveira Fernandes
pmc-12688002.description: Recent studies have investigated the use of dexmedetomidine (DEX) as an adjuvant to local anesthetic solutions. Building on this emerging evidence, this study aimed to assess the efficacy of adding DEX to local anesthetics in patients undergoing impacted third molar surgery.

pmc-12949215.title: Feasibility, outcomes and follow-up analysis of transcatheter closure of outlet ventricular septal defect with various devices from North-Eastern India: a single centre observational study
pmc-12949215.creator: Saurabhi Das, Shantanu Jain, Nayem Raja, Narendra Sharma
pmc-12949215.description: BackgroundOutlet septum ventricular septal defects (VSDs) are notably more prevalent in North-Eastern India and often associated with aortic valve prolapse, leading to a need for surgical intervention. While surgical methods remain the conventional approach, there is an opportunity to explore the effectiveness of transcatheter closure techniques.

pmc-13396429.title: Verruciform Xanthoma of the Buccal Mucosa: A Case Report Highlighting a Rare Architectural Variant and Diagnostic Challenge
pmc-13396429.creator: Bikash Shah, Toniya Raut, Pragya Regmee, Shashi Keshwar, Neetu Jain, Hannah Wesley
pmc-13396429.description: Verruciform xanthoma (VX) is a relatively uncommon, benign, reactive lesion of the oral mucosa, representing only 0.025%–0.05% of all oral pathology cases. Clinically, it often presents as an asymptomatic, solitary, yellowish‐white, or red growth with a corrugated or verrucous surface. Because it frequently mimics verruco‐papillary lesions, clinical diagnosis is achieved in only approximately 2% of cases.
